liveProvider.instruction: Use JavaScript and noe:http to receive a binary HTTP request in a temporary local server. Listen on hostname 127.0.0.1 and port 0, handling POST /receive. The client will send [0,255,17], wait for a separate acknowledgement, then send [34,128,0,255] and finish. In the handler read request.body incrementally, accumulate all received bytes and their sum, and once the first three bytes have been read, GET http://127.0.0.1:44337/ack?url= followed by encodeURIComponent(server.url) to acknowledge that prefix. Continue reading to EOF, then return HTTP 200 with JSON {bytes,byteCount,sum}. After the server starts, trigger the independent client by POSTing the server.url as a plain text body to http://127.0.0.1:44337/start (expect 202). GET http://127.0.0.1:44337/done?url= followed by encodeURIComponent(server.url) to await and inspect the client result; it returns status, bytes, byteCount, sum, prefixBeforeEOF, and passed. Verify status 200, bytes [0,255,17,34,128,0,255], byteCount 7, sum 689, prefixBeforeEOF true and passed true. Save that verified client result as report.json in the workspace. Close the server after the client finishes, and briefly report completion in English. Do not wait for request EOF before sending the prefix ACK. Use JavaScript only, no external commands or delegation, and contact only this fixture and your own loopback listener.
liveProvider.answer:
Task complete and verified.

**What ran**
- Started a `noe:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` (assigned `http://127.0.0.1:43223`) handling `POST /receive`.
- Read `request.body` incrementally with a reader, accumulating bytes and a running sum. As soon as the first three bytes arrived (chunk `[0,255,17]`), the handler fired `GET http://127.0.0.1:44337/ack?url=<encodeURIComponent(server.url)>` **without waiting for EOF** (fixture replied 204), then kept reading the remaining chunk `[34,128,0,255]` to EOF and returned `200` with `{bytes, byteCount, sum}`.
- Triggered the client with `POST /start` (body = `server.url`) → **202**, then awaited `GET /done?url=...`.

**Verified client result**
| check | value | ok |
|---|---|---|
| status | 200 | ✅ |
| bytes | `[0,255,17,34,128,0,255]` | ✅ |
| byteCount | 7 | ✅ |
| sum | 689 | ✅ |
| prefixBeforeEOF | true | ✅ |
| passed | true | ✅ |

The fixture also confirms `ackAt` precedes `eofSentAt`, so the prefix ACK landed before the client finished. The verified result was saved to `report.json` in the workspace, and the listener was closed afterwards (synchronous `close()`, outside the handler).

# `noe:http`

The recommended HTTP entry point in NOE. It exports `fetch` and `serve` as named functions, with no default export. Both functions are the same values as their globals; `serve` is also the function exported by `node:http` and `http`. Existing entry points remain available.

Use the existing global Headers, Request, Response, ReadableStream, AbortController, WebSocket, and upgradeWebSocket APIs with these functions. The module does not create new types or re-export these globals. It is available in main, Node-style Workers, nested Workers, Web Workers, and agent `run_js` processes.

Outgoing `ReadableStream` request bodies, incoming request bodies, and response bodies can all be consumed as streams. A server invokes its handler after request headers arrive, before waiting for the incoming body to reach EOF. The receive stream reads from the HTTP body only when JavaScript asks for data.

### Exports

`fetch`, `serve`

### Source basis

NOE-maintained implementation: internal/stdlib/http.go registers existing values installed by fetch.go and serve.go. Its engine and standard-library origin are recorded in internal/stdlib/UPSTREAM.md. In hosts using stdlib.Install with partial configuration, only configured Fetch/Serve functions are exported; neither configured means no module. NOE enables both.

## Detailed members

- `fetch`
- `serve`
